lines.trans: They say CEO Byun and Joon-mo traded harsh words and the set turned into a total mess.
The 2 Days & 1 Night team has not even arrived back yet—where did you pick up that news so fast?
I just heard it while escorting the department director to church service.
Do you go to church?
Ever since the department director changed.
With the previous director, did you not join a Buddhist hiking club and do temple stays?
When leadership changes, there is way more than one or two things you have to change.
I am waiting on standby here, and once the division head finishes Mass, I have to pick him up in front of the cathedral.
Because of Cindy, I have to write a statement for the Broadcast Standards Commission.
Off you go—even when Joon-mo loses his temper, he is too soft-hearted and regrets it within fifteen seconds anyway.

examples.trans: He is our company's president.
I will speak as the representative.

examples.text: 우리 가위바위보 해서 서로 짐 들어 주기 할까요?
examples.trans: Shall we play rock-paper-scissors to carry each other's bags?

examples.text: 서로 준비하면 좋은 결과가 있을 거예요.
examples.trans: If we prepare (each other), we will get good results.

examples.text: 변 대표랑 준모랑 서로 쌍소리 오가고 촬영장 아주 개판 됐대요.

examples.text: 아무튼 저 촬영장에서도 피디님만 보고 가요. 수고하세요.
examples.trans: Anyway, I am going to the set counting only on you. Keep up the good work.

examples.text: 아니 촬영장까지 와서 지금 뭐 하시는 겁니까?
examples.trans: Wait, what on earth are you doing coming all the way onto our filming set?

examples.text: 변 대표랑 준모랑 서로 쌍소리 오가고 촬영장 아주 개판 됐대요.

examples.trans: They say CEO Byun and Joon-mo traded harsh words and the set turned into a total mess.
Here the word for 'total chaos, shambles' is key.

examples.trans: The 2 Days & 1 Night team has not even arrived back yet—where did you pick up that news so fast?

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children

examples.text: 그런 실수는 누구나 할 수 있어요.
examples.trans: Anyone can make a mistake like that.
This is the first time I'm hearing a story like that.
Did you hear about this news and?
I was busy today because of news and.
Where is the restroom?
Where are you right now?
Please don't say it like that.
It's not that difficult compared to what I thought.

examples.text: 1박 팀 아직 도착도 안 했는데 너는 그런 소식을 어디서 그렇게 재빠르게 접했냐?
examples.trans: The 2 Days & 1 Night team has not even arrived back yet—where did you pick up that news so fast?

examples.trans: The 2 Days & 1 Night team has not even arrived back yet—where did you pick up that news so fast?
This expression comes from 'did you hear?'.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.
Director-nim.
Director's office.

examples.text: 다들 기다리고 계셔서 모시고 오라고 해서요.
examples.trans: Everyone is waiting, so they sent me to escort you over.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 모시다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (escort, accompany (humble)).

examples.text: 나 지금 국장님 모시고 예배 갔다 들었지.
examples.trans: I just heard it while escorting the department director to church service.
Here the word for 'worship service' is key.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!
Listen well.
Listen to a song.
I go to church every Sunday.
I met a friend at church.

meanings.en: to go around, to attend, to commute
meanings.note: Indicates regular movement or carrying something around constantly.

examples.trans: I commute to the company.
I carry a bag around with me.

examples.text: 나 마음 바뀌기 전에 빨리 계약서 보내는 게 좋을 거예요.
examples.trans: You had better send the contract quickly before I change my mind.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 바뀌다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (changing).

examples.text: 너 전번 국장이랑은 불교 산악회 다니지 않았냐, 템플스테이 막 하고?
examples.trans: With the previous director, did you not join a Buddhist hiking club and do temple stays?
Here the word for 'previous, last' is key.

examples.text: 너 전번 국장이랑은 불교 산악회 다니지 않았냐, 템플스테이 막 하고?

examples.text: 너 전번 국장이랑은 불교 산악회 다니지 않았냐, 템플스테이 막 하고?
examples.trans: With the previous director, did you not join a Buddhist hiking club and do temple stays?
Here the word for 'hiking club' is key.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

examples.text: 너 전번 국장이랑은 불교 산악회 다니지 않았냐, 템플스테이 막 하고?
examples.trans: With the previous director, did you not join a Buddhist hiking club and do temple stays?

meanings.note: used in 막을 내리다 / 막 내리다 ('to bring down the curtain', i.e., to end a show or era)

examples.trans: The performance came to an end.

examples.text: 정권 바뀌면 바꿀 게 한두 가지가 아니에요.

examples.text: 나는 빵빵빵빵이 좋은데 네가 바꾼 거 아냐.
examples.trans: I liked four zeros, you were the one who changed it.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.

examples.text: 정권 바뀌면 바꿀 게 한두 가지가 아니에요.

examples.text: 정권 바뀌면 바꿀 게 한두 가지가 아니에요.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.

examples.text: 여기서 대기하다가 본부장님 미사 끝나시면 성당 앞으로 모시러 가야 돼.
examples.trans: I am waiting on standby here, and once the division head finishes Mass, I have to pick him up in front of the cathedral.

examples.text: 여기서 대기하다가 본부장님 미사 끝나시면 성당 앞으로 모시러 가야 돼.

examples.trans: I am waiting on standby here, and once the division head finishes Mass, I have to pick him up in front of the cathedral.

meanings.en: to end, to finish, to be over

examples.trans: The meeting is already over.
What time does class end?

examples.text: 여기서 대기하다가 본부장님 미사 끝나시면 성당 앞으로 모시러 가야 돼.
examples.trans: I am waiting on standby here, and once the division head finishes Mass, I have to pick him up in front of the cathedral.

meanings.note: Usually followed by -e to mean 'because of'.

examples.trans: I was late because of the rain.
It's because of you.
I have to attend the Broadcast Commission meeting today.
The Broadcast Commission announced new regulations.

examples.text: 난 신디 때문에 방통위 답변서 써야 돼.
examples.trans: Because of Cindy, I have to write a statement for the Broadcast Standards Commission.
Here the word for 'written response' is key.

meanings.note: Irregular ㅡ-stem verb: 쓰다 + -어 becomes 써.
Commonly used for tools, money, or time.

examples.trans: I write in my diary every night.
I wrote my name on the very first page of the book.
Listen closely to what I explain.
I eat Korean food well.

examples.text: 잘 가라, 준모는 성질 내놓고도 맘 약해서 십오 초 만에 후회할 거면서.
examples.trans: Off you go—even when Joon-mo loses his temper, he is too soft-hearted and regrets it within fifteen seconds anyway.

examples.text: 잘 가라, 준모는 성질 내놓고도 맘 약해서 십오 초 만에 후회할 거면서.

examples.text: 잘 가라, 준모는 성질 내놓고도 맘 약해서 십오 초 만에 후회할 거면서.

examples.trans: Off you go—even when Joon-mo loses his temper, he is too soft-hearted and regrets it within fifteen seconds anyway.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.
